title: tier-2 shipped code: the MD5 context initialiser against Md5Init (0x1426a5100)
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is crates/ow-casc/src/blte.rs::md5_init, the initialiser the shipped md5() composes its hash from, built by cargo and called by crates/ow-casc/src/bin/verify_probe.rs through the md5_init entry. The ledger binds the verdict to blte.rs + the probe source + the git revision.

Oracle is Md5Init at exe 0x1426a5100. The body is six stores: `mov qword ptr [rcx], 0` at +0x1426a511c (the 64-bit message count) and four `mov dword ptr [rcx+8/0xc/0x10/0x14], imm32` for the RFC 1321 words (0x67452301, 0xefcdab89, 0x98badcfe, 0x10325476), then `ret`. Nothing else in the context is written, which is why the fixture fills the 64-byte buffer with non-zero patterns.

Reading note: Md5Init has no `.pdata` unwind entry (the function register jumps from Md5Final's end 0x1426a50f7 to 0x1426a5130), yet 44 call sites target 0x1426a5100 exactly and the body ends in `ret` + `int3` padding. The extent is therefore 0x1426a5100..0x1426a5124 (36 bytes through the RET); coverageWindow is that measured extent rather than the 0x2000-byte sweep ceiling, which would count the next function's branches.

The 88-byte argument is the whole client context, so the channel proves both the offsets (count at +0x00, the four words at +0x08..+0x18) and that the buffer at +0x18 survives untouched. It is the layout fn/Md5Update and fn/Md5Final operate on.

Coverage: the body has no conditional branch at all, so the sweep discovers 0 sites and the stage reports 0/0 = 100%, the same shape as fn/Md5Transform. The mutation stage carries the unit: moving a store by four bytes, swapping two words or writing a wrong constant must change one of the 88 compared bytes.
The return register is not compared: the client leaves RAX untouched, so the initialiser's value is whatever the caller had there; nothing consumes it.

acknowledgedGaps.why: The image declares no unwind record at 0x1426a5100, so the byte extent is measured from the disassembly (through the RET, 36 bytes) rather than read from `.pdata`. The address itself is not inferred: 44 call sites target it and the body is a complete store sequence ending in `ret`.
